verdict.onePlane: The planned-family film cards (P1.C1, P4.C1, P4.C2, P7.C1) fit one plane with 1.12 px rms edge error (max 2.43 px). Left out one at a time they are predicted within 2.56 px rms and the cards predicted at the 16 targets move by at most 5.4 px.
verdict.whatThatProves: Those cards were put there by the plan through the end image, so the fit shows that the generator kept the plan's own flat projection to within a few pixels. It does not show that the shot was drawn with that camera.
verdict.plan: The 16 plan quads are exactly one plane of 63 x 88 mm cards (1.1e-13 px). Against the film-calibrated plane they differ by at most 2.2 px (rms 1.2 px), which is inside the calibration's own uncertainty (2.9 px at 95 %, 5.4 px leave-one-out).
verdict.scale: Millimetres on this plane are a convention. The same plane makes a resting hand 256 mm wide and the shoe 948 mm long, and the cards the generator drew by itself measure 76 x 122 mm on it. Relative to the dealer the plan's cards are roughly half size.
verdict.use: Treating the table as one calibrated plane is sound for card positions, rendered cards, shadows and flat table artwork. Body-scale props drawn in millimetres on it will look about twice too small next to the dealer until the scale convention is settled.

limits: The landed cards of the plan clips were imposed through an end image built from the plan. They carry the plan's projection, so the plane fitted to them cannot test that projection against reality.

Four cards in three places, two of them at P4, all in the lower third of the frame. Perspective (vanishing line, focal length, height) rests on the P1 and P7 cards; P7 is partly under a hand and its far edge was read in deep shadow from the outer edge.
No real metric scale: hands, shoe and the generator's own cards disagree with the plan-scale card by factors of 1.2 to 2.6, and the older white-card take drew the P4 card about twice as wide again.
The table and the backdrop are the same green; no table outline, felt line or far corner is visible. The only table line seen is the dealer-side edge behind the hands.
Light: only the sideways lean is observable. Lean toward or away from the camera, the lamp's size and its distance cannot be separated from the unknown height of the hand.
Shadow matte: table only; nothing on cards or under the hand; one clip and one frame range. The first frames of a clip are brighter than the rest, so mattes must be normalised per frame as done here.
Principal row, lens distortion and rolling shutter are not observable; the footage is generated and need not obey one camera at all.
wouldSettleIt: A clip or still from the same READY framing with a printed grid or ruler mat lying on the table, covering P1 to P7 and the dealer-side edge, drawn by the generator without a warped end image: gives the plane and the scale the generator itself uses.
Failing that, real-size cards left where the generator puts them at P1, P4, P7 and in front of the dealer (four or more unedited landings spread over the table).
One object of known height standing on the table in the same light (a chip stack or a card box at P4 and near the shoe): fixes the light's lean toward the camera and its size.
A decision on the scale convention: either the plan card is 63 mm and the dealer is a large figure, or the dealer is life size and the cards are scaled up by about 1.2 to 2.
